title: Houston Shooting Passengers Contradict ICE Account; Dispute Agent's Position
excerpt: Passengers in the van driven by Lorenzo Salgado Araujo told their attorney that no ICE agent was directly in front of the vehicle before shots were fired, and that shots came from the sides — contradicting the government's self-defense claim.
content:
Attorney Hugo Balderas, representing two of the three passengers in the van driven by Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, held a press conference on July 10, 2026, in which he described what his clients witnessed during the July 7 ICE shooting in Houston.

'They confirmed that at no point was there ever an ICE agent directly in front of the vehicle,' Balderas said. 'They also confirmed that the shots came from the sides, not from the front, which is inconsistent with the ICE statement.' This directly contradicted DHS's account that the agent fired in self-defense after Salgado Araujo attempted to run him over.

  • Balderas also stated that his clients were feeling pressure from ICE agents to sign self-deportation papers while in custody.
  • The attorney for the passengers said the families 'will forever be physically and emotionally scarred by this.'
  • ICE had removed the agents involved from the Houston area after the shooting, but did not immediately confirm whether they remained on active duty.
  • Federal investigators had still not released the identities of the agents involved, blocking local law enforcement from conducting a parallel investigation.
